steps.transposing: Transposing moves music to another key. Every note keeps its degree, so it’s the same music, only higher or lower. {e} is degree 3 of {c} major; in {g} major, degree 3 is {b}.
steps.oneNote: Work out the note’s degree in {c} major, then find that degree in the new key. The new tonic is marked.
steps.melody: A melody moves the same way, note by note. Think of it in degrees, not in note names, and it’s easy to carry to any key.
steps.aMelody: Move each melody to the new key, note by note, in order.
steps.why: Singers do this all the time, to bring a song into their range: it’s what the app does when you sing. Pianists do it to play along with others.
steps.further: Further from home now: the same work, with more sharps and flats.
